name: North Carolina
nameStory: Carolina is Latin for 'land of Charles,' honoring King Charles I and later his son. The single colony grew too big and unruly to govern from one place, so in 1712 it was cut in half - which is why there are two Carolinas and not one.
capitalStory: Raleigh is named for Sir Walter Raleigh, who never came to America but sponsored the Roanoke colony on this coast. Those settlers vanished, leaving only the word CROATOAN carved on a post. North Carolina's capital honors the man behind the Lost Colony.

majorFeatures.name: Blue Ridge Mountains
majorFeatures.note: The high western edge of the state

majorFeatures.name: Great Smoky Mountains
majorFeatures.note: Shared with Tennessee along the crest

funFacts: Mount Mitchell, at 6,684 feet, is the highest point anywhere in the United States east of the Mississippi.
The waters off Cape Hatteras are called the Graveyard of the Atlantic; more than 5,000 ships have wrecked there.
The Wright brothers made the first powered flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903, choosing the spot for its steady wind and soft sand.
The Outer Banks are not anchored to anything - they roll slowly toward the mainland, taking roads and houses with them.
whyItMatters: On February 1, 1960, four Black college students sat down at a segregated Woolworth's lunch counter in Greensboro and refused to leave. Within two months the sit-in tactic had spread to 55 cities in 13 states.
